title: An Address to Scattered Israel
summary: An address calls on the house of Israel, including those broken off, driven out, and scattered abroad, and on the isles and distant people to listen. The speaker says the Lord called him from the womb and made mention of his name.

explicit_facts.text: The address includes people broken off and driven out because of the wickedness of the pastors of the speaker’s people.
The address includes those scattered abroad who belong to the house of Israel.
The speaker calls on the isles and people from far to listen.
The speaker says the Lord called him from the womb and made mention of his name from his mother’s bowels.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The address can be presented without showing a physically assembled audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The address speaker’s identity, appearance, and physical setting are unspecified.
The appearance and locations of those addressed are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Hearken, O ye house of Israel, all ye that are broken off and are driven out because of the wickedness of the pastors of my people;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: Listen, O isles, unto me, and hearken ye people from far;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: the Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the identified first-person narrator, but the verse does not identify him as the speaker of the address or place him physically in the scene.
The scattering and calling from the womb are reported in the address, not shown as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the address speaker as Nephi.
Do not depict a divine appearance or invent speech from the Lord.
Do not stage a birth, prenatal calling, expulsion, or scattering as a present event.
Do not invent a physically assembled audience, actions by the pastors, or additional dialogue.

title: The Servant Addressed
summary: Nephi describes himself through figurative sword, shadow, shaft, and quiver imagery and reports being addressed as a servant and as Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The first-person narrator describes his mouth as like a sharp sword and himself as a polished shaft, hidden in the shadow of a hand and in a quiver.
The narrator reports words addressing him as a servant and as Israel, in whom the speaker will be glorified.
The supplied verses do not name the speaker of the reported address.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The weapon and hiding imagery is figurative rather than a description of visible transformations.
unspecified_visual_details: No physical setting, appearance, clothing, or staging is specified.
The reported speaker's identity and appearance are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

narration.text: And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the narrator under the explicit chapter-level instruction; these two verses alone do not supply his name.
The address is reported speech, not an independently narrated present encounter.
The address “O Israel” does not establish another physically present character.
prohibited_inventions: Do not literalize the sword, hand, shaft, or quiver imagery.
Do not invent an identity or visible appearance for the reported speaker.
Do not stage the reported address as a new present-time encounter.
Do not add another person named Israel.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he has labored in vain and spent his strength for naught and in vain.
Nephi says his judgment is with the Lord and his work with God.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's appearance, location, audience, and specific labor are not described.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the speaker under the request's explicit identification of the first-person narrator; the verse does not independently name him.

prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported labor as a separate event.
Do not invent an audience, specific labor, or additional dialogue.

title: The Servant and the Light
summary: The passage describes a servant formed by the Lord to bring Jacob again to him, with God as the servant's strength though Israel is not gathered. The Lord declares the servant's calling to restore Israel and be a light to the Gentiles.

explicit_facts.text: The passage describes the Lord forming the servant from the womb to bring Jacob again to him.
Though Israel is not gathered, the servant shall be glorious in the Lord's eyes, and God shall be the servant's strength.
The Lord speaks of raising up the tribes of Jacob and restoring the preserved of Israel.
The Lord promises to give the servant as a light to the Gentiles and as his salvation unto the ends of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A text-based presentation can convey the calling and promises without depicting their fulfillment.
unspecified_visual_details: No physical setting, appearance, clothing, or staging is specified.
The servant is not named in these verses.

spoken_dialogue.text: It is a light thing that thou shouldst be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the ends of the earth.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi's identification as the chapter's narrator does not establish the identity of the servant in the quoted passage.
These verses describe a calling and promises, not their visible fulfillment.
The light to the Gentiles is figurative language, not a narrated visible transformation.
Listed characters are textual participants, not an assertion of physical presence together.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the servant as Nephi or another named person.
Do not invent a visible appearance of the Lord or a face-to-face encounter.
Do not depict gathering, restoration, or worldwide salvation as occurring here.
Do not depict the servant literally becoming light.
Do not stage the formation from the womb as a new present-tense event.
Do not place Jacob, Israel, or the Gentiles physically in the scene merely because they are mentioned.

title: The Lord’s Promise to the Servant
summary: The Lord addresses one despised by man, abhorred by the nation, and a servant of rulers, foretelling that kings shall see and arise and princes shall worship because the Lord is faithful.

explicit_facts.text: The declaration is attributed to the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One.
The addressee is despised by man, abhorred by the nation, and a servant of rulers.
Kings shall see and arise, and princes shall worship, because the Lord is faithful; these responses are foretold rather than narrated as occurring.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The declaration may be presented as text without staging its delivery.
unspecified_visual_details: No location or physical setting is established.
The addressee’s identity and appearance are unspecified.
No visible appearance of the Lord or individual rulers is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the Lord that is faithful.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: Thus saith the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One, to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth, to servant of rulers:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse attributes the declaration to the Lord but does not describe a visible appearance or a staged encounter.
The rulers’ responses are prophetic, not present action.
The narration preserves the supplied wording “to servant of rulers:” without adding an article.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an appearance of the Lord or invent a present encounter.
Do not stage kings arising or princes worshipping as events occurring now.
Do not assign identities, biographies, or relationships to the unnamed addressee or rulers.
Do not invent a physical location or depict Nephi as physically present.

title: A Covenant of the People
summary: The Lord declares that he has heard and helped the addressed “thee,” with “O isles of the sea” included in the address. He promises preservation and his servant for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth and cause inheritance of desolate heritages, so that the addressee may speak to prisoners and those in darkness. He declares that they shall feed in the ways and have pastures in high places.
characters: The Lord (quoted speaker; no visible appearance described)

explicit_facts.text: The passage introduces the words with “Thus saith the Lord:” and includes “O isles of the sea” in the address.
The Lord declares that he has heard “thee” in an acceptable time and helped “thee” in a day of salvation.
The Lord promises to preserve “thee” and give “thee” his servant for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth and cause inheritance of the desolate heritages.
The purpose clause concerns speaking to prisoners to go forth and to those sitting in darkness to show themselves.
The Lord declares that they shall feed in the ways and that their pastures shall be in all high places.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A nonliteral presentation of the quoted words can avoid staging the promises as events already happening.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, physical appearances, and visual presentation are unspecified.
No visible appearance of the Lord or his servant is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: and I will preserve thee, and give thee my servant for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: That thou mayest say to the prisoners: Go forth; to them that sit in darkness: Show yourselves.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is the explicitly identified quoted speaker; Nephi's narration does not make Nephi the speaker of the Lord's words.
Retain the source's singular “thee” without assigning a more specific identity to the addressee.
“That thou mayest say” expresses purpose, not merely permission.
These declarations do not narrate a present release, journey, feeding, or visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a homecoming or way-home framing.
Do not stage the promised events as occurring now.
Do not invent an appearance for the Lord or his servant.
Do not identify the servant or addressee beyond the supplied wording.
Do not invent prisoners' identities, dialogue, or biographies.

title: A Promise of Guidance
summary: The verses promise relief from hunger, thirst, heat, and sun; guidance by springs of water; and mountains made a way and highways exalted.

explicit_facts.text: They shall not hunger or thirst, and heat and sun shall not smite them.
One who has mercy on them shall lead them and guide them by springs of water.
The first-person voice promises to make the mountains a way and exalt the highways.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Springs, mountains, and highways may appear as illustrative imagery, not as a journey or transformation happening now.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of those being guided are unspecified.
No present setting or physical appearance for the first-person voice is specified.

narration.text: They shall not hunger nor thirst, neither shall the heat nor the sun smite them; for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them.
And I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are promises, not a narrated journey or a visible transformation.
The verses do not establish Nephi as physically present or identify him as the speaker of the first-person promise.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a present journey, a newly formed road, or a visible divine figure.
Do not invent identities, appearances, or dialogue for the people mentioned.

title: A Call to Rejoice
summary: The passage foretells people coming from afar, the north, the west, and the land of Sinim. It calls for rejoicing, foretells that the feet of those in the east shall be established and that they shall be smitten no more, and declares the Lord’s comfort and mercy.

explicit_facts.text: The passage addresses the house of Israel and foretells people coming from far, from the north, from the west, and from the land of Sinim.
The passage calls on the heavens, earth, and mountains to rejoice or sing.
The feet of those in the east shall be established, and they shall be smitten no more.
The Lord has comforted his people and will have mercy upon his afflicted.

unspecified_visual_details: No present setting or visible participants are specified.
No appearance is given for the Lord or for the people mentioned.

Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth;
for the feet of those who are in the east shall be established;
and break forth into singing, O mountains;
for the Lord hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The arrivals and establishment are foretold, not narrated as present events.
The calls for heaven, earth, and mountains to sing are exhortations, not narrated visible events.
The supplied verses do not identify the speaker of this passage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the foretold arrivals as already occurring.
Do not depict heaven, earth, or mountains literally singing.
Do not invent a visible appearance of the Lord or assign the passage’s speech to Nephi.

title: Zion's Fear Answered
summary: Zion says the Lord has forsaken and forgotten her. The passage says he will show that he has not, then contrasts a woman who may forget her child with the Lord's promise not to forget the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: Zion says the Lord has forsaken and forgotten her.
The passage says he will show that he has not.
The Lord says that even if women may forget their children, he will not forget the house of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words can be presented without showing Zion, the Lord, a woman, or a child.
unspecified_visual_details: No setting or physical appearance is specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me—
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Zion

spoken_dialogue.text: For can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee, O house of Israel.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: but he will show that he hath not.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The woman and child form a rhetorical comparison, not a narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the comparison as an event or invent an appearance for Zion or the Lord.
Do not assign the Lord's first-person promise to Zion.

explicit_facts.text: The addressee’s children will make haste against destroyers, and those who made the addressee waste will go forth.

unspecified_visual_details: The addressee, children, destroyers, and those who gather are not visually described.
